notes: READ IN FULL 21 September 2026 from arXiv:2107.11160v4 (20 Oct 2021, 17 pages) at literature/sources/eliahou-fromentin-simonetto-2021-falling-time-arxiv-2107.11160v4.pdf. The earlier record said hal.science was refused by egress policy. IT IS NOT REFUSED: hal.science returns 200 with a body reading 'Making sure you are not a bot', which looks like a successful fetch and is not one. The HAL SEARCH API is open and gave both the arXiv id and the published DOI in one call. Published version doi 10.1007/978-3-031-10796-2_7, not read. DEFINITIONS. jp(n) = T^(l)(n) with l the number of binary digits of n -- OEIS A368877, as this register recorded -- and ft(n), the falling time, the least number of jumps taking n below itself, A368878. sft is the Syracuse falling time, odd terms only. Section 1 confirms 'glide' as the computational community's name for the analogue of the stopping time for the slow map C, maintained by Roosendaal; the laboratory's own mapping of glide to dropping time was right. RESULTS. Proposition 2.1: ft(n) <= 14 for all n in [1, 2^44 - 1] with n = 3 mod 4. Proposition 2.3: the smallest 24-persistent n with ft(n) > 14 is n_0 = 1008932249296231, with ft = 15, sigma = 886 and binary length 50; it is the glide record g30. Conjecture 2.4: there is B >= 16 with ft(n) <= B for all n >= 3, a strong form of Collatz. Proposition 3.6: sft(n) <= 9 on [3, 2^35 - 1] for n = 3 mod 4, and sft <= 10 on all 34 known glide records. Conjecture 3.7: there is C >= 10 with sft(n) <= C for all n = 3 mod 4. Proposition 4.1: ft(2^l - 1) <= 5 for all 2 <= l <= 500000 outside l in {5,6}; Conjecture 4.2: ft(2^l - 1) <= 4 for l >= 133. Proposition 4.3 and Conjecture 4.4: sft(2^l - 1) = 2 for all l >= 4625. CONJECTURE 5.1, the bold one: ft(n) <= 4 for all n >= 2500 -- at most four jumps to fall below n. Conjecture 5.2: sft(n) <= 2 for all odd n >= 25000. Computations on the CALCULCO platform, SCoSI/ULCO. THE TITLE'S 12, PRECISELY. It is not the ordinary falling time. Conjecture 3.7 is stated for the SYRACUSE falling time with C >= 10, and the text then takes 'C = 12 to be on a safer side. Whence the title of this paper.' A first reading in this session attached the 12 to ft; it belongs to sft. WHY IT MATTERS HERE. Falling time is this laboratory's dropping time. Paper B's apparatus counts the words whose dropping time exceeds the word length, and the Juggler analogue is A094778. A conjecture that the falling time is bounded by an absolute constant is the sharpest possible form of the question the survivor census measures -- and its status is CONJECTURE on computational evidence plus a heuristic, not a theorem, so it constrains nothing here and must not be cited as a bound. Same Eliahou as eliahou-1993-collatz-cycle-lengths, eliahou-2011-cycles-non-triviaux-iii and eliahou-verger-gaugry-2025.
title: Is the Syracuse falling time bounded by 12?
